question: The hand signal for 'Single File' is given by:
choice_a: Extending the arm and index finger straight up
choice_b: Extending the arm straight down, palm back
choice_c: Extending the arm out, palm up
choice_d: Tapping the top of the helmet
explanation: Single File: arm and index finger extended straight up.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Double File' is given by:
choice_a: Arm extended straight out, palm down
choice_b: Arm with index and middle finger extended straight up
explanation: Double File: arm with index and middle finger extended straight up.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Stop' is given by:
choice_a: Arm extended out, palm up, swinging upward
choice_b: Arm extended upward 45 degrees, palm forward
choice_c: Arm extended straight down, palm facing back
choice_d: Open and close hand with fingers extended
explanation: Stop: arm extended straight down, palm facing back.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Speed Up' is given by:
choice_c: Fist clenched with an up-and-down motion
choice_d: Arm extended straight out, palm facing up, swinging upward
explanation: Speed Up: arm extended straight out, palm facing up, swing upward.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Slow Down' is given by:
choice_a: Arm extended straight out, palm down, swinging down to your side
choice_b: Arm extended upward from the shoulder, palm forward
choice_c: Tapping the top of the helmet with an open palm
choice_d: Pointing to the fuel tank with a finger extended
explanation: Slow Down: arm extended straight out, palm facing down, swing down to your side.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Follow Me' is given by:
choice_a: Arm extended straight down, palm back
choice_b: Arm extended straight up from the shoulder, palm forward
explanation: Follow Me: arm extended straight up from the shoulder, palm forward.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'You Lead/Come' involves:
choice_c: Arm extended upward 45 degrees, palm forward, swinging in an arc from back to front
choice_d: A single finger pointed forward without movement
explanation: You Lead/Come: arm extended upward 45 degrees, palm forward pointing with index finger, swung in an arc from back to front.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.58, 'Hand Signals'

question: To signal a 'Hazard in Roadway' on the right side, a rider should:
choice_a: Wave the left arm in a circle
explanation: Hazard in Roadway: on the left, point with the left hand; on the right, point with the right foot.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Highbeam' is given by:
choice_a: Tapping the top of the helmet with an open palm down
explanation: Highbeam: tap on top of the helmet with an open palm down.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Fuel' (needing to stop for gas) is given by:
choice_b: Arm out to the side pointing to the tank with finger extended
choice_c: Fist clenched with a short up-and-down motion
choice_d: Open and close hand with fingers and thumb extended
explanation: Fuel: arm out to the side pointing to the tank with finger extended.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for a 'Comfort Stop' (restroom break) is given by:
choice_a: Arm swung toward the shoulder as for a right turn
choice_c: Forearm extended, fist clenched, with a short up-and-down motion
choice_d: Both hands raised above the helmet
explanation: Comfort Stop: forearm extended, fist clenched, with a short up-and-down motion.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for a 'Refreshment Stop' is given by:
choice_c: Open and close hand with fingers and thumb extended
explanation: Refreshment Stop: fingers closed, thumb to mouth.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Turn Signal On' (alerting a rider whose blinker was left on) is given by:
choice_a: Open and close the hand with fingers and thumb extended
choice_b: Point at the rider's turn signal directly
choice_c: Tap the top of the helmet
explanation: Turn Signal On: open and close hand with fingers and thumb extended.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'

question: The hand signal for 'Pull Off' is given by:
choice_a: Arm extended straight down, palm back
choice_b: Arm positioned as for a right turn, with the forearm swung toward the shoulder
choice_d: Arm extended straight up with index finger
explanation: Pull Off: arm positioned as for a right turn, forearm swung toward the shoulder.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.59, 'Hand Signals'
